# CI and releases

CI runs repository checks, package tests, protocol tests, and docs/examples in parallel. Windows checks the installed packages. These jobs do not publish.

Run **release / create-pr** on main and select **core** (CLI and both clients) or **integration-ai-sdk**, then patch, minor, or major and stable or alpha. Stable promotes the current alpha to its base version: `0.0.1-alpha.0` becomes `0.0.1`. Preview is the default. Integrations advance independently; incompatible client peer ranges require an explicit maintainer edit. Package/scope membership lives in `scripts/release/release-scopes.ts`.

Selections accumulate in one release PR on `release/next`, preserving earlier selections and human edits. Repeating a scope replaces its selection using the main baseline, without compounding bumps. After merge, the next request starts a new release cycle. Squash-merge with the generated **chore: release packages** title. The workflow explicitly starts CI because GITHUB_TOKEN-created PR events do not trigger it; if dispatch fails, run CI manually on `release/next`.

**release / publish** runs the existing CI, validates candidate artifacts, then publishes only the selected package/version set through the protected **release** environment. Dry runs never publish. Retry using the original full release SHA; already-published bytes must match and only missing artifacts are uploaded. Registry verification precedes per-scope GitHub releases, such as `core/v0.0.1` and `integration-ai-sdk/v0.0.1`.

Before the first publication, a maintainer must own the npm scope, bootstrap the three legitimate npm package records, and configure their trusted publishers, plus PyPI's pending publisher. Use repository **ranst91/remote-skills**, workflow **publish-release.yml**, environment **release**. Configure main-only deployment and the intended human approval policy. Registry setup is external; adding these workflows does not complete it. npm OIDC supports private repositories, but npm provenance requires a public repository. After making the repository public, verify its publishing provenance and environment protection before the official release.

The packaging job builds and verifies three npm tarballs plus the Python wheel and source distribution. It starts with private empty caches, prepares declared dependencies, and installs the artifacts offline. The retained candidates also run the existing CLI/cross-language smoke and deterministic AI SDK browser scenarios. Publication downloads that same verified bundle. These checks make no paid model calls and require no alpha release.

For a one-time registry check, set `REMOTE_SKILLS_E2E_PACKAGES` to an absolute JSON manifest path and run `node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/examples/end-to-end.test.ts tests/examples/vercel-ai-sdk.test.ts`. The manifest supplies `npm: [{name, version, spec}]` for all three npm packages and `python: {version, spec}`; use exact `name@version` / `remote-skills==version` specs or absolute `.tgz` / `.whl` paths. Each test installation verifies versions and local resolution. Registry-alpha checks are not a permanent CI precondition.

After a verification-tooling fix, start a new **release / publish** run on main with the original release SHA. Current verification tooling checks out that immutable source separately, so fixes to CI do not change the release's packages or versions. Re-running an old failed workflow would still use its old tooling.
